A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Tighter Performance Theory of FedExProx and contain readable main text, equations, figures, algorithms, and complete appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 8 and Figures 1–4 report original empirical time-complexity experiments on synthetic quadratic and smooth-hinge classification problems.

after.justification: Section 8 and Appendix G retain the synthetic experiments and add original ARCENE classification results in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The FedExProx updates, partial-participation algorithm, GraDS and StoPS extrapolation rules, and inexact-proximal variant are retained. Additional experimental documentation does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix G.3.2 adds smooth-hinge classification on a subset of ARCENE, extending the previous synthetic-only coverage to one real dataset. The original quadratic and synthetic classification tasks remain.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparison method is added or removed. The retained plots compare FedExProx settings and theoretical versus empirical costs; the ARCENE experiment introduces no competing algorithm.

E3.justification: The added ARCENE experiment introduces random selection of 20 observations and 30 features. Existing synthetic client counts, local GD procedures, extrapolation selection, and cost metrics remain unchanged; newly stated stopping and timing settings are disclosures rather than established revisions.

E4.justification: Figure 5 adds a sensitivity study testing whether the time-versus-gamma behavior under different communication costs persists on real data. The earlier partial-participation sweeps and theoretical-versus-empirical analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The added experiment does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds ARCENE time-complexity curves showing a nonzero optimal gamma and increasingly pronounced U-shaped behavior as communication costs rise. Figures 1–4 retain their existing result curves; their resizing and relabeling do not represent performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects the reformulated objective from an average of Moreau-envelope gradients to an average of Moreau envelopes. The principal assumptions, convergence guarantees, and proofs remain unchanged; the communication-cost renaming and new contraction-factor shorthand are equivalent notation.

C1.justification: Contribution 5 explicitly qualifies the PŁ extension as applying to convex functions, matching the existing theorem assumptions. The conclusion newly states an explicit priority claim for rigorously demonstrating an advantage over GD. The central convergence and communication-cost claims remain.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly characterizes the GD comparison as primarily pedagogical. Appendix G.1 explicitly justifies counted computation and communication as a controlled wall-clock proxy, while G.3.2 interprets the ARCENE curves as support beyond synthetic examples.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly documents Gaussian/QR generation of quadratic matrices, eigenvalue sampling, synthetic classification data generation and labeling, tau = 1, and an objective-gap stopping threshold of 10^-3. It also supplies the ARCENE source and subsampling details. These improve documentation without establishing reruns of retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guyon et al. (2004) for ARCENE and makes the claimed priority of the GD comparison explicit in the conclusion. The existing optimization references and substantive positioning relative to earlier FedExProx work are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Section 8 becomes Experimental Highlights, with detailed experiments moved into a newly organized Appendix G. Localized prose and conclusion rewrites, communication-cost renaming, updated affiliations and headers, and an LLM-use disclosure accompany this reorganization; the theoretical narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 move from the main text to Appendix G, and Figure 5 is added. Retained plots are resized and receive label, caption, and tick-density adjustments. The notation table retains its structure.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through the data-generation and stopping details in Appendix G, adds limited real-data support through ARCENE, and corrects the objective definition in Appendix B. These are useful but bounded gains: the core methods and guarantees are retained, and the new empirical evidence covers only 20 observations and 30 features.
